e: From syenite + -ic, from Syene, where Synetic stone was found.
Borrowed from Latin Syēnītēs, from Syēnē (“Aswan”), because it was anciently quarried there.
q: The temple, of which some massive hewn blocks and a fine column of Syenite granite still mark the site, occupied a terrace facing the source of the river and commanding a magnificent prospect.
1906, James George Frazer, Adonis, Attis, Osiris, page 15:
Much of the southern half of the southeastern body is a mafic syenite, slightly more felsic than the shonkinite.
